title: 局部避让选速与角色实际执行的区别
evidence_scope: Targeted primary-paper reading and original abstract receiving-constraint example; no avoidance implementation, game, native or physical robot execution.

sources.title: Reciprocal n-body collision avoidance
sources.bibliography: Robotics Research: The14th International Symposium ISRR, Springer Tracts in Advanced Robotics70, May2011, pp3–19.
sources.pagination: This linked author PDF has16 physical pages, numbered1–16; not mechanically mapped to book pagination.
supports: Preferred velocity, permitted-velocity choice and actual position update play distinct roles.
Empty intersection and least-violating fallback do not mean all original constraints are satisfied.
Post-clamping the selected velocity to dynamics no longer retains a strict avoidance guarantee.
sources.reading_scope: Main/editor and independent reviewers read relevant text/formulas. No paper images, project video or implementation execution.
limitations: Finite-horizon conditions under the selected simplified model, not universal progress, arbitrary asynchronous execution or initially overlapping states.
Zero optimization velocity is distinct from zero preferred velocity; candidate does not rely on that special-case strategy.
Historical scales and performance are not target-game budget evidence.

original_example.assumed_constraint: vx<=0.75m/s for this illustrative receiving step; not an observed ORCA solver output.
original_example.controller_inputs: previousvx0.9m/s; maximum decrease0.1m/s in this step
original_example.claim_limit: Demonstrates non-preservation of a stipulated constraint, not inevitable physical collision or a tested tolerance.

non_goals: Sensing, timing or acceleration error bounds
